Recommended Highlights This Week

1. BIGBANG 2026-2027 World Tour <XX: COSMOS> – 17 and 18 October, National Stadium

2. NCT 127 5th Tour ‘Neo City: The Redline’ – 18 October, Singapore Indoor Stadium

3. Avenged Sevenfold – 13 October, Singapore Indoor Stadium

4. Fan Chang Tien: Rhythm of the Southern Brush – opens 16 October, National Gallery Singapore

5. Golden Autumn Hairy Crab at Shang Palace – from 15 October

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

The Line moves into the Yunnan leg of A Journey Across China's Culinary Heartlands on 12 October, the final region of the series, which runs to 25 October. Shang Palace's A Cantonese Expression of Korea's Finest closes on 14 October, and the restaurant launches its Golden Autumn Hairy Crab menu the next day. Beng Hiang's Hokkien menu at the Garden Terrace carries on as usual, as do The Rose Veranda's An Afternoon in Japan, Origin Grill's Meat Series and the Lobby Lounge's Peranakan set dinner.

  • The Line – A Journey Across China's Culinary Heartlands (Yunnan leg, 12–25 October 2026, daily). Lunch $68++/adult, $34++/child (6–11 years); dinner $98++/adult, $49++/child (6–11 years). Shangri-La Circle members: 30% off, Monday to Friday lunch and dinner only – lunch $48++/adult, $24++/child; dinner $68++/adult, $34++/child.

  • Shang Palace – A Cantonese Expression of Korea's Finest, daily lunch and dinner. Final days – closes 14 October 2026. The regular à la carte and set menus remain available.

  • Shang Palace – Golden Autumn Hairy Crab, 15 October to 30 November 2026. Hairy crabs from Tai Hu Lake. Menu and pricing are confirmed with the restaurant directly (ext. 7460).

  • Beng Hiang – Authentic Hokkien cuisine at the Garden Terrace. Lunch 11:30am–2:30pm; dinner 6:00pm–9:30pm, daily.

  • The Rose Veranda – An Afternoon in Japan. Valid through 15 November 2026.

  • Origin Grill – The Meat Series: The Art of Aged Beef. Valid through 17 December 2026.

  • The Lobby Lounge – An Evening of Rich Peranakan Flavours, set dinner. Valid through 15 November 2026.

  • Waterfall Ristorante Italiano – Mamma Ria and Mamma Rosa Are Here, A Taste of Puglian Tradition, 30 October to 8 November 2026; with a Sunday Brunch with Mamma Ria and Mamma Rosa on 1 and 8 November.

  • Squeaky's Trick or Treat Weekend – 30 October to 1 November 2026.

  • White Truffle Season returns to Waterfall Ristorante Italiano – 10 November to 20 December 2026.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (2 adults + 2 children). Valid through 31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

  • J65 – International Seafood Dinner Buffet. $88++/adult, $44++/child. Shangri-La Circle members: 20% off.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

  • Makan@JEN – daily lunch and dinner buffet, $30–55++ per person. 15% off for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

With the Grand Prix behind us, the week opens with Avenged Sevenfold at the Singapore Indoor Stadium on Tuesday 13 October and builds into a very full weekend. Super Junior-83z play The Star Theatre on Friday 16 October. On Saturday 17 October, BIGBANG open a two-night run at National Stadium, PLAVE and ART RIOT share the Singapore EXPO precinct, and ARTBAT make their Singapore debut at Pasir Panjang Power Station. NCT 127 play the Singapore Indoor Stadium on Sunday 18 October, the same night as BIGBANG's second show. Culturally, Fan Chang Tien opens at the National Gallery on 16 October, the PEACEMINUSONE × Toy Story pop-up opens at Clarke Quay the same day, Sands Comedy Season runs at Marina Bay Sands, and Little India's Deepavali lights are on nightly. F1 The Exhibition and Art Remembers both close on 18 October.

BIGBANG 2026-2027 World Tour <XX: COSMOS>

BIGBANG's 20th-anniversary world tour brings G-Dragon, Taeyang and Daesung to National Stadium for two nights.

Event Date: 17 and 18 October 2026, 7:00pm both nights
Location: National Stadium, Singapore Sports Hub
Admission: Ticketed via Ticketmaster Singapore, $158 to $498 before booking fees
Best For: K-pop Fans / Milestone Concert

Concierge Recommendation: Expect Kallang-area congestion on both nights and advise guests to allow extra time for taxis and ride-hailing. Sunday night is busier still, as NCT 127 play the nearby Indoor Stadium at the same time.

NCT 127 5th Tour ‘Neo City: The Redline’

NCT 127 return to Singapore on their fifth world tour for a single night at the Singapore Indoor Stadium.

Event Date: 18 October 2026, 7:00pm (doors open 5:30pm)
Location: Singapore Indoor Stadium
Admission: Ticketed, $228 to $368
Best For: K-pop Fans

Concierge Recommendation: Remind guests to confirm which venue their event is at before booking transport. On Sunday 18 October, BIGBANG are at National Stadium and NCT 127 at the Indoor Stadium, both in the Kallang precinct and starting at 7:00pm.

Avenged Sevenfold

The American rock band play Singapore as part of their 2026 Asia tour. Nene Royal, the Thai guitarist and singer who won America's Got Talent Season 21, opens the show.

Event Date: 13 October 2026, 8:00pm
Location: Singapore Indoor Stadium, 2 Stadium Walk
Admission: Ticketed, $128 to $258
Best For: Rock and Metal Fans

Concierge Recommendation: The week's first big concert, on a Tuesday night, so it is a good one to mention to guests who want a live show before the weekend crowds arrive.

Super Junior-83z – ‘1983’ Fancon

Super Junior-83z bring their debut fancon tour, ‘1983’, to Singapore for one night at a seated venue.

Event Date: 16 October 2026, 7:30pm
Location: The Star Theatre, Buona Vista
Admission: Ticketed via Ticketmaster, $178 to $298 before booking fees
Best For: K-pop Fans

Concierge Recommendation: Tickets went on general sale in May, so availability may be limited; suggest guests check Ticketmaster early. Buona Vista MRT is the nearest station.

PLAVE World Tour ‘Keep It Manic’

PLAVE are a five-member virtual idol group who perform live through real-time motion capture and live vocals, which makes this a genuinely different kind of K-pop concert.

Event Date: 17 October 2026, 3:00pm
Location: Apex @ EXPO, Singapore EXPO
Admission: Ticketed, from $158 before booking fees
Best For: K-pop Fans / Anyone Curious About Virtual Idols

Concierge Recommendation: Worth mentioning to guests as a curiosity. It is an afternoon show at the Singapore EXPO, so it suits guests who want a concert without a late night.

ART RIOT 2026: Villains & Ne’er Do Wells

Singapore's fandom-focused art and pop-culture market returns this weekend with a theme built around villains.

Event Date: 17 October, 12:00pm–8:00pm; 18 October, 11:00am–7:00pm
Location: Hall 6B, Singapore EXPO
Admission: Ticketed via Eventbrite
Best For: Families / Anime and Pop-Culture Fans / Art Collectors

Concierge Recommendation: A good lower-key alternative for guests who want weekend atmosphere without a concert-sized crowd. PLAVE play at Apex @ EXPO the same afternoon, so the EXPO precinct will be busy on 17 October.

ARTBAT – Singapore Debut

The Ukrainian electronic duo play their first Singapore show at Pasir Panjang Power Station, a cinematic techno set after dark.

Event Date: 17 October 2026, evening
Location: Pasir Panjang Power Station
Admission: Ticketed, general admission from $128; VIP Stage Passes include access behind the DJ booth, fast-track entry and a dedicated bar
Best For: Electronic Music Fans / Nightlife

Concierge Recommendation: A late-night event well outside the city centre, so advise guests to arrange return transport in advance, as ride-hailing demand will be high when the event ends.

Sands Comedy Season

The second edition of Marina Bay Sands' comedy season runs across three headline shows at Sands Theatre.

Event Date: Mark Lee, ‘Old Horse Still Have Spring 2.0’ – 16 and 17 October, 8:00pm; Xiaoguo Comedy, ‘Stand-Up Comedy and Friends Season 3 World Tour’ – 18 October, 3:00pm; Liang Hai Yuan, ‘Three Nights of Genius’ – 18 October, 8:00pm
Location: Sands Theatre, Marina Bay Sands, 10 Bayfront Avenue
Admission: Ticketed via the Marina Bay Sands website; Mark Lee from $38 to $128, the other two shows $68 to $198
Best For: Comedy Fans / Chinese-Speaking Guests

Concierge Recommendation: The shows are billed under their Chinese titles, so confirm the language of performance before recommending them to guests who do not speak Mandarin.

Fan Chang Tien: Rhythm of the Southern Brush

A retrospective of more than 70 paintings, calligraphy works, poems, seal carvings and archival materials following Fan Chang Tien's journey across Guangdong, Shanghai, Bangkok and Singapore. The exhibition presents him as a scholar-artist, poet and philanthropist, not only the ‘Gardener’ who nurtured Singapore artists.

Event Date: 16 October 2026 to 31 January 2027, daily 10:00am–7:00pm (last admission 30 minutes before closing)
Location: Wu Guanzhong Gallery, Level 4, City Hall Wing, National Gallery Singapore, 1 St Andrew’s Road
Admission: General Admission ticket required; free for Singapore citizens and PRs
Best For: Art Lovers / Culture-Minded Guests

Concierge Recommendation: A strong rainy-day or daytime recommendation, and it can be paired with Art Remembers in the same building before that closes on 18 October.

PEACEMINUSONE × Toy Story: The First Fan Pop-Up

G-Dragon's PEACEMINUSONE label brings its Toy Story collaboration to Singapore, with a Singapore-only collection of T-shirts, hats and tote bags that combines PEACEMINUSONE's daisy motif with Toy Story characters.

Event Date: 16 October to 11 November 2026, daily 1:00pm–9:00pm
Location: CQ @ Clarke Quay
Admission: Entry passes are $12 each and are currently sold only with pre-orders from the wider collection on the official website; general sale is to follow. Each pass includes a tote bag.
Best For: Fans of G-Dragon / Collectors

Concierge Recommendation: Relevant to BIGBANG fans staying with us. Merchandise is limited to three pieces per product per customer and is not sold online, so advise guests to check how to obtain a pass before they go.

Deepavali Lights and Festival Village, Little India

Little India's Deepavali lights stretch over 2 kilometres of Serangoon Road and are switched on every evening, while the Festival Village on Campbell Lane runs through to Deepavali itself.

Event Date: Lights nightly 7:00pm–midnight; Festival Village 10 October to 8 November 2026, from 7:00pm. Deepavali falls on Sunday 8 November.
Location: Little India – Serangoon Road and Campbell Lane
Admission: Free
Best For: Culture-Minded Guests / Photography / Evening Strolls

Concierge Recommendation: A free, walkable evening away from the concert crowds. On Sunday 18 October, Lembu Road, Kerbau Road, Chander Road, Dunlop Street and Birch Road are closed to vehicles from 12:00pm to midnight, so guests arriving by car or taxi should be dropped off nearby.

Last Chance This Week

  • F1 The Exhibition – Gardens by the Bay MRT Plaza. Closes 18 October. Admission fee applies.

  • Art Remembers – National Gallery Singapore, City Hall Wing Level 3. Closes 18 October. Daily 10:00am–7:00pm; General Admission ticket required.

  • Stories of Everyday – National Museum of Singapore. The celebration for the reopened Singapore History Gallery closes 18 October; the gallery itself stays open daily, 10:00am–7:00pm.

Also This Week

  • Halloween Horror Nights 14 – Universal Studios Singapore, Resorts World Sentosa. Thursday to Sunday, 7:30pm–12:30am, on 18 select nights until 1 November. From $68.

  • Horizon of Khufu: Journey in Ancient Egypt – Parkview Square, 600 North Bridge Road. A VR experience, daily 10:00am–6:00pm, until 2 April 2027. $35 adult, $29 child under 8.

Restaurants & Bars

Ojeje

Ojeje is a Seoul tonkatsu and udon specialist and this is its first restaurant outside Korea. The pork is wet-aged before breading and the udon is made fresh in-house. The original branch near Seoul Station reportedly draws 60 to 80 waiting parties a day.

Location: #B1-12, Raffles City Shopping Centre, 252 North Bridge Road, Singapore 179103 (beside City Hall MRT)
Status: Now open. Daily from 11:00am; last orders 9:00pm
Signature: Pork Loin Katsu with Kadaif Prawn Set, $38; Premium Matcha Zaru Udon, $17; Carbonara Udon (Singapore exclusive), $22
Note: Not halal-certified

Concierge Recommendation: A genuine queue-puller based on its Seoul record. Suggest an early or off-peak visit in its first few weeks, and note that the Raffles City location suits guests coming from the hotel by MRT.

Tanica

A live-fire restaurant at The Singapore EDITION on Cuscaden Road, serving a weekday three-course lunch and a Sunday semi-buffet brunch.

Location: The Singapore EDITION, 38 Cuscaden Road, Singapore 249731
Prices: Weekday three-course lunch $48++; Sunday semi-buffet brunch from $98++
Telephone: +65 6329 5000
Note: Not halal-certified

Concierge Recommendation: A convenient Orchard-side option for a weekday business lunch or a relaxed Sunday brunch.

Bari Bari Grand

A premium offshoot of a Hong Kong chain, serving hot-stone grilling and teppan dishes at The Capitol Kempinski.

Location: #01-82, Arcade @ The Capitol Kempinski, 15 Stamford Road, Singapore 178906
Hours: Daily 11:00am–10:00pm
Signature: Miyazaki wagyu ribeye, $75++
Note: Not halal-certified

Concierge Recommendation: A good fit for guests who like interactive dining and are already in the City Hall area.

Vincenzo Capuano

A pizzeria at The Pier at Robertson, on Mohamed Sultan Road, offering a 90-minute lunch buffet.

Location: #01-12, The Pier at Robertson, 80 Mohamed Sultan Road, Singapore 239013
Hours: Daily 12:00pm–3:00pm and 6:00pm–11:00pm
Prices: Lunch buffet $28++ (90 minutes)
Telephone: +65 6845 9153
Note: Not halal-certified

Concierge Recommendation: A relaxed, casual option for families and groups looking for a simple Italian meal.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La’s Restaurant Recommendation List

One pick this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Shisen Hanten by Chen Kentaro

The first overseas outpost of the Sichuan restaurant group from Japan founded by the late Chen Kenmin, now supervised by Chen Kentaro. The menu features a few Cantonese favourites as well as Sichuan specialities, and its signature mapo doufu, silky tofu glistening in red chilli oil and dressed in a hot, spicy pepper-flavoured sauce, is the dish most guests come for. Business set lunch menus are a good way to sample the cooking.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: Reserve through the restaurant’s website (TableCheck), by telephone on +65 6831 6262 or by email; the restaurant is cashless.

Hours: Lunch Monday to Friday 12:00pm–3:00pm (last order 2:30pm); weekend and public holiday brunch 11:30am–3:15pm (last seating 1:45pm); dinner daily 6:00pm–10:30pm (last order 9:45pm).

Address: Level 35, Hilton Singapore Orchard, 333 Orchard Road, Singapore 238867

Website: https://shisenhanten.com.sg/

Signature: Mapo Tofu; handcrafted dim sum, including truffle siew mai

Concierge Recommendation: A dependable choice for guests who want Sichuan cooking in a refined setting on Orchard Road. Note the dress code: shorts and flip-flops are not permitted.

Hotel & Hospitality News

  • DoubleTree by Hilton Singapore Robertson Quay opened on 30 September at 401 Havelock Road, on the former site of Hotel Miramar. The 344-room hotel has more than 200 rooms overlooking the Singapore River, an outdoor pool, a 24-hour fitness centre and a 64-seat café and bar, Brew:33. Its all-day restaurant, SAUS, opens on 1 November. Havelock MRT is about five minutes away on foot.

Transport & Operational Updates

Road closures for the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix remain in effect until 5:30am on Tuesday, 13 October. Selected stretches reopen briefly between 5:30am and 10:00am on Monday 12 October. Normal traffic should resume around Marina Centre and the Padang from the morning of 13 October.

The Woodsville Tunnel closes overnight, 12:01am to 5:00am, for maintenance on four nights: 13 and 14 October (Serangoon Road to Upper Serangoon Road, northbound), 15 October (Upper Serangoon Road to Bendemeer Road, southbound) and 16 October (MacPherson Road to Bendemeer Road). Other overnight works include the MCE (towards ECP) from Exit 5 to Fort Road on 14 October, 12:00am to 5:00am.

On Sunday 18 October, Teck Whye Lane is closed from 6:30pm to 9:30pm between Teck Whye Avenue and Lamp Post 17 for the Nine Emperor Gods Festival. The permanent Sunday closures in Little India also apply: Lembu Road, Kerbau Road, Chander Road, Dunlop Street and Birch Road, from 12:00pm to midnight.

Expect heavier traffic and ride-hailing demand in the Kallang precinct on Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October, with BIGBANG at National Stadium on both nights, NCT 127 at the Indoor Stadium on the Sunday, and PLAVE and ART RIOT at the Singapore EXPO on the Saturday. The Star Theatre at Buona Vista on Friday 16 October is best reached by MRT.

Suggested Itineraries

A Little India Evening

Late Afternoon: Walk through Little India while it is still light, taking in the shopfronts along Serangoon Road and Campbell Lane.

Evening: Stay for the Deepavali lights, switched on from 7:00pm, and the Festival Village on Campbell Lane, which opens at the same hour.

Dinner: Round off with a meal at one of Little India's long-running restaurants.

Tip: A good option for guests who want an evening out but would rather avoid the concert crowds in Kallang and at the EXPO this weekend.

A Day of Art at the National Gallery

Morning: Start with Art Remembers, which closes on 18 October, in the City Hall Wing.

Afternoon: Move to Fan Chang Tien: Rhythm of the Southern Brush at the Wu Guanzhong Gallery on Level 4 (opens 16 October). The Gallery is open daily from 10:00am to 7:00pm.

Evening: Dinner at Shang Palace, with the Golden Autumn Hairy Crab menu from 15 October.

Tip: Both exhibitions are in the same building; the combined visit works from Friday 16 October, once Fan Chang Tien is open and before Art Remembers closes on 18 October.

A Weekend of Music

Saturday: Afternoon at the Singapore EXPO for PLAVE (3:00pm) or ART RIOT, then BIGBANG at National Stadium at 7:00pm, or ARTBAT at Pasir Panjang Power Station for guests who prefer electronic music.

Sunday: BIGBANG's second night at National Stadium, or NCT 127 at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, both at 7:00pm.

Tip: Remind guests that the venues are far apart and to confirm the venue before booking transport.

Quick Reference

Best Milestone Concert: BIGBANG <XX: COSMOS> (National Stadium, 17 and 18 October)

Best K-pop Pick on Sunday: NCT 127 (Singapore Indoor Stadium, 18 October)

Best Rock Show: Avenged Sevenfold (Singapore Indoor Stadium, 13 October)

Most Unusual: PLAVE, a virtual idol concert (Apex @ EXPO, 17 October)

Best New Exhibition: Fan Chang Tien: Rhythm of the Southern Brush (National Gallery, from 16 October)

Best Free Evening Out: Deepavali lights, Little India

Best New Restaurant: Ojeje (Raffles City)

Looking Ahead: Golden Autumn Hairy Crab at Shang Palace starts 15 October; Deepavali is on Sunday 8 November
